title: Fomo Kernel Condition Slot
description: One condition the user committed to that the engine's own metrics cannot compute (#412). The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/conditions.py holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. Two shapes appear here: `input` is what an agent may put on commitment.condition, and the rest of the document is the durable row stored in <root>/conditions.jsonl.

slot_id.description: Engine-assigned identity, derived from the session id. Slots carry their own identity and never join through session.PKEY.

kind.description: What sort of condition this is, written on every row because rows are append-only and never rewritten. numeric: a line the engine compares an observation against. event: a yes/no occurrence with no line — the agent brings evidence, the user answers, and that answer is the verdict of record. Inferring the kind from a missing threshold would be permanent and wrong the first time a numeric condition arrives without one.

criterion.description: The user's own words, stored and displayed verbatim and never translated (#396). Stating it as a yes/no threshold is correct and is never rewritten.

query.description: A neutral factual lookup, authored once at commit time and frozen for replayability. Never the criterion restated as a question: a yes/no lookup biases retrieval toward confirmation, returning a real event, a real source, and a wrong date. The engine refuses a query carrying threshold.value.

created.description: The review's date_end, matching a rules.jsonl row's `created`.

session_id.description: The session that created the slot.

tier.description: Derived from evidence by the engine, never declared by an agent. derived = computed from the user's own trade records; fetched = external feed (prices today); researched = agent lookup, adjudicated with two-sided reasoning; unmapped = committed to, and honestly not watchable.

unmapped_reason.description: Present exactly when tier is unmapped, and the three differ in what the user should be told. no_threshold: the criterion carries no numeric line, so it cannot be checked mechanically at all. no_baseline: it is watchable in principle, but nothing was found to anchor it, so it is currently blind. no_adjudicator: an event condition, whose verdict is the user's to give — the flow that asks is not built yet.

threshold.description: The comparison, structured — so the engine performs it rather than an agent asserting the answer.

unit.description: Free text as the user means it: %, USD, x, days.

direction.description: Which side of the line means the condition is met.

near_line.description: Margin, in threshold units, inside which a not-yet-met condition still deserves a question. Frozen at creation: left adjustable it becomes a hidden lever over how often the user is asked. Defaults to 10% of |threshold.value|, and is required when the threshold is zero (a line at zero has no magnitude to take a fraction of). Zero disables the band rather than pinning it to exact equality.

baseline.description: What was found at commit time. Kept on every row that has it, watchable or not: it is what someone actually looked up, and dropping it would leave the record thinner than the conversation that produced it.

baseline_verdict.description: The engine's comparison at commit time. `met` means the user has committed to a line that is already crossed — a decision to make now, not a tripwire to watch.

revises.description: The parent slot_id this row revises, present when the user's criterion was re-stated. Absent on a line's root row. Engine-assigned; never accepted on `input`.

line_id.description: The stable identity of this slot's line — the slot_id of the line's first row. A revision changes slot_id but keeps line_id, so re-stating a criterion does not read as a brand new condition. Root rows written before this field existed have no line_id on disk; identity falls back to slot_id (conditions.slot_line_id mirrors problems.rule_line_id). Engine-assigned; never accepted on `input`.

thesis_cycle_id.description: #416 C2: the position cycle whose thesis this condition falsifies, present when the slot was created from a thesis_updates row's exit_trigger. Engine-assigned from that row's own cycle_id and never accepted on `input` — an agent able to name the cycle could attach a condition to a thesis the user never wrote. A revision inherits it from the row it revises. Once that cycle is no longer a held position the row stops being due and stops raising questions; it is never rewritten or deleted.

input.description: What an agent may place on answers.commitment.condition. Everything else in this document is engine-assigned; supplying it is an error.

observation.description: One evidence record. source + as_of is the same provenance anchor #414's public_fact tag requires and the price envelope already uses.

as_of.description: The date the figure describes, not the date it was read.

period.description: Period identity (fiscal quarter, month). Half of what a later check uses to tell new information from the same period re-worded.

document.description: Document identity (filing, release). The other half.
